newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Parliament expels Kuwaiti anti-Israel protester.
newsitem.headline: Parliament expels Kuwaiti anti-Israel protester.

text.p: Kuwaiti parliament security men on Tuesday expelled a lone protester who chanted "Death to America, Death to Israel" from the public gallery.
The man, Western-educated Omran Mohammad, was escorted outside when, in violation of house rules, he chanted from the gallery while parliament was in session.
"God is bigger than America," declared Mohammad, a research scientist and human rights activist.
He earlier told reporters that the governorate of Kuwait City had turned down a request by 186 people, including 14 MPs, to gather outside parliament on Tuesday to protest against Israeli policies.

The group included Sunni Moslem and Shi'ite members, Islamists and liberals who failed to show up for a rally inside parliament. Nine people briefly joined Mohammad in chanting "God is Great, Death to Israel, Death to America" outside the parliament complex.

Kuwait does not have direct relations with Israel and refuses to normalise ties with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for appearing to side with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf Arab state.

As in most Arab and Moslem countries, the start of work last month on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem triggered strong condemnation in Kuwait, which has agreed with other Arab states to stop moves towards normalisation of ties with Israel.
